existing.description: The Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) funds excellent research at universities and other institutions.
existing.eligibility_summary: Researchers with a doctorate and several years of research experience (2–8 years after PhD). Must not yet have achieved the objective of leading their own research project and team. Must have a Swiss link (Swiss nationality, Swiss degree, or at least 2 years research in Switzerland at 80% FTE).
benefits: * Provided that you meet all the eligibility criteria for SNSF Starting Grants, in particular the criteria relating to career stage limits (see Call Doc, Art 1.2).
The SNSF Starting Grants Call (Horizon Europe Transitional Measures) do not count towards the upper limit of concurrent projects.

existing.selection_notes: The evaluation of the submitted proposals is based on the principle of competition. Discipline-specific panels of scientists will evaluate the proposals in a two-phase procedure.
existing.duration: 5 years. Earliest project start: 1 May 2027; latest: 1 May 2028.
existing.program_type: If applicants do not request any salary, then they must be employed at least 0.5 FTE and dedicate at least 0.5 FTE to the project funded by this grant.

existing.description: When can you apply for a scholarship?
eligibility: Be in a difficult financial situation
Swiss students, C permit holders and refugees: since the 1st year Propaedeutic, or in exceptional cases since the CMS
Have received a rejection from the cantonal scholarship programme, or be awaiting a response
International students: after completing at least one year at EPFL and successful completion of the first-year cycle
International students: an unexpected and sudden change in social, family or financial situation
existing.eligibility_summary: Means-tested support for EPFL students in a difficult financial situation who have exhausted or are awaiting cantonal and other funding; Swiss/C-permit/refugee students may apply from the 1st year Propaedeutic, international students only after at least one year at EPFL and successful completion of the first-year cycle.
benefits: Monthly scholarship of up to CHF 2,600
Awarded for 5 or 10 months per academic year
Renewable each academic year by re-applying
coverage: Means-tested monthly living-cost grant, maximum CHF 2,600 per month
Awarded for 1 or 2 semesters (5 or 10 months) per academic year
requirements: Apply for the cantonal scholarship first and send the acknowledgement of receipt
Application submitted on the official EPFL form with all documents listed on it
Swiss/C permit/refugee track or international track conditions as applicable
documents: Financial and social situation evidence as listed on the official form
Acknowledgement of receipt of the cantonal or state grant application, where applicable
Copy of the signed rental contract once accommodation is secured
application_method: Download the official DOCX application form from the scholarship page
Complete the budget and situation sections
Send the completed file with all supporting documents to the EPFL social team
existing.selection_notes: Decisions are taken by the EPFL Social Commission, which "meets 5 or 6 times a year", after the subsidiarity test.
existing.best_fit: EPFL enrolled students (Swiss, C permit, refugee or international) whose financial situation has deteriorated and who have already been refused cantonal or state aid.
existing.notes: Students living in the canton of Geneva, or who applied to the Geneva cantonal scholarship office (SBPE), must apply through the Hans Wilsdorf fund box instead of this scholarship.
existing.duration: 1 or 2 semesters (5 or 10 months) per academic year, renewable each year
existing.application_period: Rolling twice-yearly windows; the 2025-2026 applications "are now closed"
existing.deadline_display: New / renewal application: 01.12.2026, then 15.02.2027, for support starting from the autumn semester 2027
